status: keyboard retention and mounting prototype; physical load and fit tests required

carrier.material: 1.2 mm annealed 304 stainless steel; confirm HRB 90 maximum for SP clinch nuts
carrier.insulating_film: DuPont Kapton 500HN, 0.127 mm nominal, without added adhesive thickness
carrier.mechanism_window_note: The PCB copper-exclusion rectangles are conservatively continued through the steel. This is an additional carrier precaution, not a claim that the PCB drawing specifies a backing-plate construction.

side_supports.material: 1.5 mm aluminum, HRB 80 maximum for the selected S clinch nuts
side_supports.root_fasteners: four M2 x 4 pan screws, four small washers and four captive DIN 934 M2 nuts
side_supports.carrier_fasteners: four M2 x 5 pan screws, four small washers and four PEM S-M2-1 nuts
side_supports.washer_note: Fit allocation to match the purchased washer. The mounting joints are clamped, not qualified thermal-expansion slides.

retention.material: insulating clips; select material after warm fit and load tests
retention.screws: eight M2 x 6 DIN 965 countersunk screws
retention.head_note: The cone covers the theoretical 90 degree profile. Match the actual countersink and seating height to the purchased screw.
retention.nuts: eight PEM SP-M2-1 in the steel carrier
retention.clip_fit_note: Measure the assembled PCB, film and clips before tightening. Adjust the clip seating height rather than forcing a warped or thicker board into the nominal gap. Deburr the metal and confirm electrical isolation.

center_stop.note: Replace the ordinary H22 mounting screw with this spacer. The existing PCB mounting pad is backed by the base support. Set the insulating cap to the measured 0.2-0.4 mm unloaded gap; this is a local deflection stop, not a plate-stiffness qualification.
